Breaking: 10 Spies More Lethal Than James Bond

📅 28 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2300 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Screenrant

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Few literary spies are as synonymous with danger and lethality as James Bond.
  • Sources indicate that james Bond may be the poster child for dangerous fictional spies, but in reality there are plenty who make him look relatively tame.
  • Industry observers note that surviving the massacre of a presidential protection detail is an unusually brutal introduction to a thriller protagonist.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Few literary spies are as synonymous with danger and lethality as James Bond. Ian Fleming’s 007 literally has a license to kill, proving that a capacity for violence isn’t just part of his job description, it’s one of his greatest professional strengths. Across Fleming’s 14 James Bond books and the dozens of continuations from other authors that followed, M16’s most famous spy permanently dispatched countless foes in a variety of painful and creative ways.

Sources indicate that james Bond may be the poster child for dangerous fictional spies, but in reality there are plenty who make him look relatively tame. The Bond of the novels is far less trigger-happy than his movie counterpart, but the same can’t be said for the generations of thriller spies he inspired. Plenty are far more lethal than 007, with the most dangerous completing missions through means Fleming’s vision of Her Majesty’s Secret Service would never allow.

Industry observers note that surviving the massacre of a presidential protection detail is an unusually brutal introduction to a thriller protagonist. That’s precisely how readers encounter Scot Harvath in Brad Thor’s The Lions of Lucerne, which establishes that his character has much more depth than his Secret Service credentials. Before protecting presidents, Harvath served as a Navy SEAL. His subsequent career in covert counterterrorism after the death of his security team combines both backgrounds, creating an operative who understands how protection works and possesses the military skills to dismantle it.

Sources indicate that throughout his series, Scot Harvath fights multiple sustained campaigns of violence under conditions that should finish him. For example, 2019’s Backlash strips away his support and leaves him fighting through hostile Russian territory, turning his survival skills and appetite for revenge into an especially vicious combination. It’s not uncommon for Harvath to kill dozens of people in a single novel. This is especially true when his friends and family are at risk and things get personal. Bond is dangerous when cornered, but Harvath’s special operations background makes pursuing him an exceptionally costly mistake.

You can purchase The Lions of Lucerne, the first Scot Harvath novel by Brad Thor, here.

An art restorer hardly sounds like the obvious choice to outclass 007. The civilian profession of author Daniel Silva’s Gabriel Allon, however, suits a killer whose defining qualities include patience, precision, and extraordinary attention to detail. Recruited into Israeli intelligence after the 1972 Munich Olympics massacre, Allon participated in the campaign to eliminate those responsible. His background establishes him as a specialist in targeted assassination long before the first novel in his series, 2000’s The Kill Artist, begins, with the consequences of that work following him throughout Daniel Silva’s novels.

According to recent reports, gabriel Allon is a notably lethal spy when he’s dealing with his targets up close. Daniel Silva describes his early assassinations as close-range shootings with a .22-caliber Beretta, emphasizing nerve and preparation over overwhelming firepower. He’s not a literary spy that only has violence to rely on, however. Allon’s linguistic abilities and talent for assuming convincing identities make reaching the target part of the same skill set as killing them. Whereas meeting James Bond isn’t an encounter those in his orbit forget in a hurry, Gabriel Allon knows how to become completely unremarkable until he makes his move. The fact that various organizations try to bring him back to his career as an assassin despite him wanting to leave that life behind is further testament to just how lethal he truly is.

You can purchase The Kill Artist, the first Gabriel Allon novel by Daniel Silva, here.

It has been revealed that losing his memory should make Jason Bourne an easier target. Instead, 1980’s The Bourne Identity introduced readers to a covert operative whose survival instincts and skills remain terrifyingly effective even after he’s forgotten honing them. Author Robert Ludlum builds much of the suspense of the Jason Bourne novels around that contradiction: the titular spy knows how to survive a world full of professional killers, but can’t remember how he acquired his lethal skillset. Bourne’s level of combat conditioning is so deep and thorough that his training kicks in on a subconscious level.

The novels also give Jason Bourne a considerably wider skillset than a straightforward assassin. Robert Ludlum’s original trilogy places Bourne in an elaborate operation that requires deception and infiltration just as much as armed and unarmed combat. Later authors expand the violence, placing Bourne against rival assassins and intelligence organizations equipped to anticipate his methods. Across those different incarnations, Bourne proves himself much more dangerous than 007 thanks to his incredible adaptability. Removing his support network, compromising his identity, or sending trained operatives after him never seems to make him any less of a threat.

You can purchase The Bourne Identity, the first Jason Bourne novel by Robert Ludlum, here.

The distinction between merely investigating terrorists and actively eliminating them is central to the appeal of the Mitch Rapp novels. Author Vince Flynn’s CIA operative specializes in the latter, approaching counterterrorism with a lethal urgency that repeatedly puts him at odds with his superiors. 2010’s American Assassin, which serves as a prequel, traces Rapp’s trigger-happy mentality back to personal loss and his recruitment into a covert assassination program. From there, Rapp honed himself into one of the most proficient killers at the CIA’s disposal.

It has been revealed that what makes Mitch Rapp especially frightening is his cold and calculated approach to even the most violent operations. His training encompasses all manner of firearms and close combat, but it’s his willingness to use his skills without a second’s hesitation that makes them so deadly. This is where his operations differ significantly to 007’s, and this difference reveals everything about which is the more dangerous. James Bond’s assignments frequently require him to uncover a larger conspiracy before confronting its architect. Rapp is often dispatched because the U.S. Government wants an enemy to stop breathing.

You can purchase Transfer of Power, the first Mitch Rapp novel by Vince Flynn, here.

It has been revealed that A body count only reveals so much about an assassin’s skills. Often how targets are killed matters just as much as how many have been dealt with. This makes John Rain an especially competent literary spy, since his victims often aren’t recognizable as murder victims at all. The Japanese American freelancer from Barry Eisler’s novels specializes in deaths that appear natural, making him particularly valuable to employers who need a person removed without attracting attention. Beginning with 2002’s Rain Fall, also published as A Clean Kill in Tokyo, Barry Eisler turns Rain’s ability to conceal violence the basis for one of the most lethal spies to grace the pages of a thriller novel.

As expected, the ability to make a murder look like an accident is far from the only trick up John Rain’s sleeve. Serving in the Special Forces during Vietnam and extensive martial arts experience mean he’s just as capable in an open fight as he is setting up an elaborate assassination. Still, it’s his penchant for creative and untraceable kills that define Rain. Surviving a gunfight is one thing. Arranging matters so that nobody realizes a killing occurred requires an entirely different level of control.

You can purchase A Clean Kill In Tokyo, the first John Rain novel by Barry Eisler, here.

Pike Logan belongs to an organization designed to operate beyond the normal limits of American law. In Brad Taylor’s novels, a black book group codenamed The Taskforce recruits from elite military and intelligence backgrounds. Even among a roster of highly experienced specialists, however, 2011’s One Rough Man establishes Logan as an especially lethal operative. His notably military approach makes him especially dangerous when a mission develops into a sustained confrontation.

Logan thinks about factors like surveillance, positioning, coordination, and escape as connected problems, and has no qualms about using lethal force whenever the situation demands it. Author Brad Taylor’s own Special Forces experience adds a notable level of detail that makes Logan’s professional competence feel legitimate. James Bond is an exceptional lone operative, but Pike Logan brings the tactical lethality and group-coordination of an elite military unit into the world of espionage. His lethality comes just as much from knowing how to use the people around him as it does any weapon.

You can purchase One Rough Man, the first Pike Logan novel by Brad Taylor, here.

In a recent development, most fictional spies have a life before whatever intelligence service they work for recruits them. Even the enigmatic James Bond went to Eton and served in the Navy before joining Her Majesty’s Secret Service. Evan Smoak’s preparation begins at twelve, when the Orphan Program takes him from a group home and starts conditioning him to be a highly covert government assassin on a team that doesn’t officially exist. By adulthood, Smoak’s entire world has been defined by violence, surveillance, and operational discipline. Gregg Hurwitz’s Orphan X, the first novel in the series of the same name, introduces the result: a man whose formidable resources and specialized skills make his disappearance from the organization that made him a matter of national security.

In a recent development, working as the Nowhere Man, Smoak redirects his abilities toward helping people, but that doesn’t make him any less dangerous to those who earn his attention. His lethality comes from obsessive preparation just as much as shooting or fighting. He assesses his surroundings, anticipates complications, and treats small mistakes as potential disasters, an approach that leads to watertight operation planning. James Bond is a man who has been trained for danger. Evan Smoak feels like he’s been psychologically conditioned into a living weapon.

You can purchase Orphan X, the first Evan Smoak novel by Gregg Hurwitz, here.

In a recent development, being hunted by the CIA would be a serious problem for any literary spy, including James Bond. For Court Gentry, aka The Gray Man, it becomes an extended demonstration of why the agency couldn’t simply let him walk free after his years of service. Author Mark Greaney’s former covert assassin survives long after his own employers mark him for death. He manages to build a successful career as a freelancer despite being hunted by one of the most far-reaching intelligence organizations in the world.

It has been revealed that as for why Court Gentry is more dangerous than James Bond, the central spy of The Gray Man novels has an advantage when it comes to sheer concentration of expertise. Unlike 007, who carries out a wide variety of types of missions, Gentry’s career is built on surviving encounters with other highly trained killers. Bond often comes face-to-face with dangerous foes, but this is rarely part of the blueprint. Gentry exists precisely to take out these kinds of threats. Bond may be the more well-rounded spy, but Gentry is inarguably the more lethal of the two.

You can purchase The Gray Man, the first Court Gentry novel by Mark Greaney, here.

Sources indicate that before adopting the name John Clark, John Kelly from the world of the Jack Ryan novels was a former Navy SEAL and Vietnam veteran whose personal revenge campaign develops alongside a military prisoner rescue operation. Tom Clancy gives Clark the skills for both undertakings when he made his debut in 1988’s The Cardinal of the Kremlin, and then spends multiple books showing just how ruthlessly he can apply them. Clark’s professional effectiveness comes from versatility accumulated over a long career. A potent combination of maritime, military, and clandestine fieldwork experience allows him to function across situations that demand very different kinds of expertise.

According to recent reports, john Clark’s later leadership of the multinational counterterrorism unit Rainbow showcases the full extent of those capabilities, as he turns a team of elite but disconnected specialists into a lethally coherent unit. James Bond may have formidable instincts when violence becomes the only option, but Clark’s professional capacity for it ensures that he rarely, if ever, needs to rely on anything but carefully applied brute force. He understands how to plan a mission, select the necessary people, and deliver operational success even when up against overwhelming firepower.

You can purchase The Cardinal of the Kremlin, the first novel to feature John Clark by Tom Clancy, here.

Espionage missions that heavily feature luxury, global travel, and impeccable presentation make Villanelle, aka Oxana Vorontsova, an obvious spiritual successor to James Bond. However, she doesn’t just build on his legacy when it comes to making the spy lifestyle look lavish. She also embodies the cold-blooded professional killer archetype that Ian Fleming’s 007 is often mistaken as being. Author Luke Jennings introduces Vorontsova in the Killing Eve novels as a Russian killer recruited by the secretive Twelve, whose intervention transforms an already violent young woman into an international assassin. Her handlers supply fresh identities and intensive training, turning her capacity for murder into a highly marketable professional skill.

It has been revealed that like 007, Villanelle is an extremely adaptable and capable spy. Where they differ is that she has an alarming absence of remorse. Bond’s conscience often causes him to hesitate before making a kill in the novels, or even change his mind and lower his weapon. This isn’t the case for Villanelle. What’s more, she appears to take a disturbing pleasure in this aspect of her work. Bond is only ever violent when he feels it’s necessary to complete his mission. Villanelle seems to go out of her way to find solutions that require bloodshed. This means that, naturally, she ends up killing much more frequently than James Bond ever has, and ensures she’s one of the most dangerous spies ever to appear in a thriller novel.

You can purchase Codename Villanelle, the first Killing Eve novel by Luke Jennings, here.

It has been revealed that amazon's Black Friday 2026 sale has brought the Sonos Arc Ultra down to $849 from its usual $1,099, a $250 discount that marks its lowest price yet. PCMag named it the best soundbar of 2024 and gave it an “outstanding” rating in its review. Still, $849 is a lot to spend on a single soundbar, and anyone shopping on a tighter budget will find more affordable picks in our Fire TV soundbar roundup. For more editor-vetted tech deals, check out our comprehensive Black Friday coverage.

For those who can make room in their budget, the next thing to plan around is space, since the Arc Ultra measures a little over 46 inches across and weighs about 13 pounds, making it a natural match for a larger TV. Despite all that width, it keeps a low profile at just under three inches tall, so it can sit beneath most screens without blocking the picture, or you can wall-mount it if you would rather keep your TV stand clear. All that size makes room for a 9.1.4-channel layout (a substantial step up from the original Arc) that gives Dolby Atmos effects more space to spread around and above you. Sonos also added a latest Sound Motion driver that it says doubles the original Arc's bass, giving action scenes real weight without a separate subwoofer, though you can still add a Sub 4 later for more rumble.

At the other end of the sound spectrum, voices and dialogue come through clearly even at low volumes, and a Speech Enhancement mode lifts them further. Trueplay tuning then adjusts the sound to your room, with a quick version on Android and iOS and a more detailed one for iPhone owners. The biggest drawback is connectivity, since the Arc Ultra has a single HDMI eARC port with no passthrough, which can leave you short on inputs for a console or streaming box, and no optical port. It also lacks DTS:X support, a letdown for some Blu-ray collectors, and voice control is limited to Alexa or Sonos' own assistant, though Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and AirPlay 2 make streaming music from your phone easy.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. The best thing you can do is compare the prices with other retailers that have Black Friday sales. If that seems like too much work, you can just follow our Black Friday coverage (we're already doing all the searching and vetting for you). Electronic products now pack circuits, structures, thermal paths, and packaging into very small spaces. These physical domains interact with one another. A packaging choice can change how a shock load reaches a circuit board. Such interactions are hard to predict. Most are found during physical qualification, late in development. At that stage, the design is mostly fixed. A failure leads to redesign, rebuilds, and retesting. Physical tests give strong evidence of robustness, but they give limited insight into load paths and failure margins. Traditional simulation gives more detail, but it needs specialist skills and long manual setup. This white paper explains how guided virtual validation brings shock and drop assessment into the design phase. It reviews common test configurations, model inputs, and acceptance criteria. A packaged drop case study then reveals how packaging can be optimized across all drop orientations and checked against physical test results.

Tech Report: Tokenization platform Securitize gains 10% postmarket on Q3 results, move into asset-backed finance

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (449 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.
  • Industry observers note that miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively new corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure.
  • The growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.

Industry observers note that miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively new corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure. Tokenized assets on the platform grew 9% in the third quarter, to $4.8 billion, from the same period a year ago. Aggregate transaction volume rose 20% from a year ago, to $4.3 billion. Revenue of $11.5 million was up 28% from last year.

The growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept. 17, which created a temporary pathway for trading of certain tokenized stocks and strengthened the regulatory outlook.

Profitability is still meaningfully below year-ago levels, due in part to costs associated with going public over the summer, as well as the scaling up of the tokenization business at an active time for the entire sector, Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo told CNBC in an exclusive interview.

Industry observers note that securitize reinforced "certain areas of the company like finance, compliance, legal [and] cybersecurity," which increased corporate costs "compared to a year ago when we were privately held," Domingo said. "We're in in a very good position. The adjusted EBITDA … is improving significantly from previous quarters.".

Recent findings suggest that securitize reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of $2 million, compared with positive adjusted EBITDA of $3.6 million a year ago, better than a $5.5 million loss in the second quarter. The manufacturer posted a 183% increase in operating costs and expenses.

In a recent development, also on Monday, the Securitize board authorized a $50 million share buyback and announced the acquisition of River One, an institutional asset-backed financing platform developing technology to connect stablecoin capital with traditional lending markets. Terms were not disclosed.

Securitize sees an opportunity to modernize the $9 trillion market for asset backed finance by using stablecoins to finance real world assets, generate yield and tokenize investment positions and credit products, Domingo mentioned.The acquisition also marks an expansion beyond Securitize's core niche markets at a time when tokenization's competitive landscape is growing, with traditional asset managers like BlackRock and Franklin Templeton, and established financial market infrastructure providers like DTCC and Broadridge, entering the industry.

"We have been very active in tokenized funds, treasuries [and] yield … And we've been obviously recently very active in tokenized stocks, so this adds another piece of the puzzle in the emerging tokenization space for us to capture revenue growth.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • FRIDAY AM: Lionsgate‘s The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping saw the second best Thanksgiving and Thursday of the franchise with $11.6M after Catching Fire‘s $14.95M 13 years ago and ahead of Mockingjay Part 2‘s $11M in 2014.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

FRIDAY AM: Lionsgate‘s The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping saw the second best Thanksgiving and Thursday of the franchise with $11.6M after Catching Fire‘s $14.95M 13 years ago and ahead of Mockingjay Part 2‘s $11M in 2014.

Sources indicate that the running cume of the sixth feature adaptation of the Suzanne Collins series is $174.9M with an $85M 5-day still within reach. Yesterday, the fifth Francis Lawrence directed Hunger Games pic flew past the $166.3M lifetime cume its predecessor, 2023’s Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes‘ $166.3M. Sunrise on the Reaping‘s running total by Sunday looks stand around $233M, which will be 17% ahead of Mockingjay 2 at the same point in time and +3% ahead of Mockingjay 1. Both titles respectively ended their domestic runs at $282M and $337.1M. The highest grossing Hunger Games title is Catching Fire with $425.3M.

In a recent development, all pics at the Thanksgiving Box Office rang up an estimated $35.6M, -9% from last year’s Thanksgiving. Business is expected to go up to $59M on Black Friday, a busy moviegoing day — but it’s not going to be as busy as last year when all titles minted $75M, boosted by Zootopia 2 and Wicked for Good. Watch on Deadline.

Universal/Paramount’s Focker In-Law was second yesterday with $7.7M at 3,382 theaters, putting its 5-day at $40M for second place.

Sources indicate that disney’s Hexed continues to be cursed with a $4.5M Thanksgiving at 3,725 which was higher than Wish‘s $3.8M Turkey Day but lower than Encanto‘s $5.8M. The Walt Disney Original Animation Title continues to see a $35M 5-day in third place. Disney execs may want to make a trip to the Obsession magic shop today in nearby North Hollywood, buy a Wish Willow and wish for better grosses on Hexed.

Angel Studios’ Hershey officially opened yesterday with a combined day and preview gross of $2.9M at 2,275 theaters, 3-day of $5M and 4-day of $8M in 7th place. The Alexandra Daddario and Finn Wittrock movie is seeing its best grosses in the South with 27% of its gross there. Pic is also playing to norms in East, Midwest, South Central and Mountain. The Penn Cinema in Lititz, PA is Hershey‘s top gross with $31K so far; that a 41-minute drive from Hershey, PA.

Recent findings suggest that netflix’s The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth is losing his mustache with a $590K Thursday, and lower $2.3M 3-day and $3.75M 5-day at 252 theaters in 8th. The David Fincher directed, Quentin Tarantino sequel movie is 79% certified fresh with Rotten Tomatoes critics, down from the 86% of its predecessor, the 2x Oscar winning Once Upon a Time in Hollywood. Those who watched the part 2 of the Brad Pitt movie gave it an 88% on RT, which is very good and higher than Once Upon a Time in Hollywood‘s 70% — it’s just not being found in a major way by male dudes. Theater average over 5-days is $14,880 still better than Wake Up Dead Man‘s $7K a year ago.

In a recent development, neon’s Paper Tiger which is also making a play at specialty house men, but at much lower cost than Cliff Booth, $15M to $200M in production costs, posted a $340K Thanksgiving, on track for a 3-day of $1.65M, 5-day of $3M in its expansion from 28 theaters to 1,332 theaters in 9th place. Neon acquired Paper Tiger before Cannes where the James Gray directed crime noir received a 10 minute standing ovation at its premiere. RT audiences at 66% aren’t far from the pic’s C+ CinemaScore. Not an audience pleaser.

In a recent development, THANKSGIVING AM PATCH: An alpha female property, Lionsgate’s The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping with a continued 5-day forecast of $85M+, is stealing business from two other female-leaning movies at the Thanksgiving box office, Universal/Paramount’s Focker In-Law and Disney’s Hexed, both of which are coming in lighter than their forecasts with 5-days of $36M and $35M respectively. That’s essentially a fight for 2nd over the Wednesday-Sunday stretch at this point in time.

Sources indicate that now, that’s not to say that it was silly to date other female pics on top of another tentpole, however, the holiday has shown that two exceptionally pleasing events for the demo can coexist at the same time, read 2024’s Moana 2 and Wicked and even last year’s Wicked: For Good and Zootopia 2. Hexed and Focker In-Law aren’t exceptionally pleasing.

Industry observers note that most movies are expected to ease on average -23% today off their Wednesday daily B.O. as families ease back for festivities. Tomorrow, Black Friday, should see a daily surge between 50%-100% for most titles.

According to recent reports, sunrise on the Reaping‘s $15.1M Wednesday is the second best in the Suzanne Collins’ franchise after 2013’s Catching Fire which did $20.8M on the day before Thanksgiving. 3-day is still on track for $58M+, -51%.

Focker In-Law saw an uptick in its franchise CinemaScore to B+ from previous chapter, 2010’s Little Fockers which received a B-. The original movie 26 years ago has the best grade of A-. The pic is alright with a 64% definite recommend in Screen Engine/Rentrak PostTrak exits. Yesterday was $5.3M with the 3-day at $24.8M. Half of the audience was 18-34 yesterday, 46% over 35 and 64% female overall. Diversity demos were 37% Caucasian, 33% Latino and Hispanic, 13% Black, 10% Asian American and 7% Native American/other. PLFs rep 17% of the gross so far with the John Hamburg directed sequel (the first two pics were helmed by Jay Roach, the third by Paul Weitz) playing best in the West, South, and South Central. AMC Burbank is the top venue with $21k. Again, the Uni and Paramount co-production cost $90M net before global P&A.

Recent findings suggest that disney’s $200M Hexed is waiting for a box office spell tomorrow that could raise this original animated movie above the doldrums of the studio’s Thanksgiving 2023 dud Wish ($175M production cost, $8.1M Wednesday, $19.6M 3-day, $31.6M 5-day and final domestic of $63.9M). Hexed made $7.6M yesterday (including Tuesday previews) and is eyeing a 3-day of $20M. Hexed gets an A- just like Wish did. PostTrak shows 62% definite recommend for the general audience while kids under 12 gave it a 96% in the top 2 and a 51% must see right away. Kids under 12 rep 31% of the audience while 35-44 (parents) revealed up at 31%. Diversity demos were 48% Caucasian, 26% Latino and Hispanic, 9% Black, 7% Asian American and 9% Native American/other.

Again, there are no original songs in this movie about a mother and daughter witch, the latter who realizes her powers as both are transported into another portal where they are trying to save their own kind from doom.

It has been revealed that like Focker-in-Law, Hexed is sharing PLFs with Sunrise on the Reaping which owns most of the holiday supply, those screens are counting 17% of the animated pic’s holiday B.O. so far. 3D is driving 12%. West, South, South Central, Midwest and Mountain are the best markets with the East soft performing 2% below the norm this week. AMC Dine-In Disney Springs Florida is the best location with $52k.

Paramount’s Ebenezer is looking at 4th place at 3,180 theaters with $1.6M yesterday, and still $6.8M-$7.3M third weekend, -6% to -13%, for a 5-day of $10M-$10.6M and running cume on the high end of $45.9M.

Fifth is Amazon MGM Studio’s I Play Rocky with $1.4M yesterday at 2,711 sites, $6.6M 3-day, -29%, 5-day of $9.6M and total of $22.6M by EOD Sunday.

It has been revealed that outside the top 5 is Netflix’s The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth at 252 locations, boosted by AMC Imax. Wednesday’s opening day estimate was $910K, 3-day is looking at $3.3M and a 5-day of $4.85M. At that level, the theater average over 5-days is $19,2K which is higher than what Netflix pulled did last Thanksgiving with Wake Up Dead Man: A Knives Out Mystery which had a per theater of $7K. Note that Rian Johnson directed thriller was booked in more theaters at 600 sites. Still a bit more robust result here on a limited basis than Wake Up Dead Man ($4.25M 5-day), but alas, Netflix, you’re leaving soooo much money on the table and there’s more than a enough room in this marketplace to have gone wide and minted at least $20M for this sequel to beloved fan Quentin Tarantino pic Once Upon a Time in Hollywood which at $142.8M is the Oscar winning filmmaker’s second highest grossing movie at the domestic B.O. Cliff Booth filmmaker David Fincher told Collider that the pic cost $120M-$123M, not $200M. We’ll leave it to Wall Street to figure out the downstream.

According to recent reports, there’s a shot that Neon’s third weekend wide expansion of James Gray’s crime noir, Paper Tiger, based on the filmmaker’s life, comes in higher than Cliff Booth. Wednesday was an estimated $950K which translates into a $4.4M 3-day, 5-day of $5.1M at 1,322 (+1,294) theaters. Running total by Sunday is around $5.7M. Audiences weren’t wild about the Miles Teller, Adam Driver and Scarlett Johansson movie giving it a C+.

Industry observers note that angel Studio’s Hershey biopic about the chocolate maker with Alexandra Daddario and Finn Wittrock got a leg up with early shows yesterday with $1.3M including $534K estimated previews. No firm projection yet, but it was always expected to file in the single digits over its ‘4-day’ start. The pic doesn’t officially open until Thursday and all that preview cash will be rolled into day one. CinemaScore audiences love it with an A, and PostTrak isn’t shabby with 83% positive and a 69% definite recommend, but critics didn’t have a sweet tooth for it 17% Rotten. Male-to-female turnout was 50/50 with the Angel faithful attending at 37% over 55, and 51% over 45. Diversity demos are 61% Caucasian, 17% Black, 13% Latino and Hispanic, 6% Asian American, and 3% Native American/other.

WEDNESDAY AFTERNOON: If extreme weather doesn’t shutter theaters in the Northeast, then Lionsgate is looking forward to a lucrative Thanksgiving stretch with The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping potentially banking $85M+ over five-days.

Should the sixth title in the Suzanne Collins series file in that range, it will rep the second best Thanksgiving haul for a Hunger Games movie after Catching Fire‘s $109.9M Wednesday-Sunday turkey take 13 years ago. Sunrise on the Reaping‘s Wednesday is looking like $15.5M-$16.5M with a second 3-day weekend around $58M-$65M at 4,018 theaters, -46% to -51%. Five day forecasts are always a challenge for the industry to predict: Business dips on Thanksgiving then spikes on Black Friday, which is one of the most active moviegoing days of the year. By Sunday, we’re looking at a running cume for the Francis Lawrence directed movie of $233M domestic, which would be 40% higher than the lifetime cume on 2023’s Hunger Games: Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes.

According to recent reports, second will either be Disney’s Hexed at 3,725 theaters or Universal/Paramount’s Focker-in-Law at 3,382 sites. Hexed is seeing around $7.8M today (including $2.1M previews), for a 3-day around $20M and 5-day between $35M-$40M. Let’s see if this picks up before passing complete judgement on this $200M original animation production, but it’s clear Hexed isn’t Coco or Frozen.

Focker In-Law is seeing a $5.2M Wednesday, 3-day of $24.8M and 5-day of $36.1M. No Rotten Tomatoes audience scores yet on either title.

Fourth goes to Paramount’s third frame of Johnny Depp Christmas movie, Ebenezer with $1.5M today at 3,180 sites and a 3-day between $6.8M-$7.3M, -6% to -13%, for a 5-day of $10M-$10.6M and running cume on the high end of $45.9M.

Fifth is Amazon MGM Studio’s fourth frame of I Play Rocky at 2,711 with $1.4M today, 3-day of $6.6M, and 5-day of $9.5M for a running cume of $22.5M.

Outside the top 5 is Netflix’s Once Upon a Time in Hollywood sequel, The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth at 251 locations with $1M today, $3M 3-day and 5-day of $5M.

WEDNESDAY AM: As we told you last night, Lionsgate scored its best Tuesday ever at the domestic box office with The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping and the best ever for the Suzanne Collins franchise as the day raked in $15.98M.

2013’s The Hunger Games: Catching Fire owned the previous best Tuesday for the franchise with $15.96M. Running cume for the fifth Francis Lawrence movie is $148.1M and by Thanksgiving, Sunrise on the Reaping will surpass its previous 2023 chapter’s lifetime domestic B.O. of $166.3M.

Recent findings suggest that as we told you, Sunrise on the Reaping will dominate the Thanksgiving Wednesday through Sunday stretch as the franchise has historically done before since 2013, this time with a floor of $70M+. Previously, the pics over Thanksgiving cooked up the following: Catching Fire ($109.9M), Mockingjay Part 1 ($82.6M), Mockingjay Part 2 ($75.9M) with Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes way behind ($42.2M).

Lionsgate has had back-to-back global hit openings this year with Sunrise on the Reaping last weekend at $226.1M WW and Michael with $218.8M. This has all happened under the administration and watch of Motion Picture Chairman, Adam Fogelson. Still no word out there whether or not Lionsgate rejected or accepted Legendary’s bid.

Walt Disney Animation’s Hexed came in with $2.1M, $100K above the $2M we were spotting yesterday. That preview figure is higher than Encanto ($1.5M previews, 5-day of $40.5M) and Wish ($1.8M previews including $500K Saturday sneaks; 5-day of $31.6M). No RT audience score yet, but critics were meh at 67% fresh. There is a chance that the traditional Disney pic comes in lower than its 5-day forecast of $40M-$45M as original animated titles are very challenging to launch in the streaming era, but you have to start some place.

Sources indicate that universal and Paramount’s Focker In-Law, which didn’t have previews last night, rather began showtimes at midnight, has more potential to hit its 5-day forecast of $45M given the Ariana Grande factor and the fact that audiences love the franchise. The first Meet the Parents 26 years ago was the fave among critics at 85% fresh on Rotten Tomatoes. Focker-in-Law isn’t the worst at 26%, as that belongs to 2010’s Little Fockers. 2004’s Meet the Fockers stands at 39%.

Hexed, Focker-in-Law and Sunrise on the Reaping are sharing PLFs with the latter having Imax screens (except for AMC where they are being designated to Netflix’s The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth).

In a recent development, thank God for Lionsgate Hunger Games at the box office: Sans a Wicked, Moana and a Zootopia, the Thanksgiving box office will certainly be down from last year’s five day robust $290.3M, which was the fifth best ever. Moana 2 and Wicked led the holiday to its best haul ever with $424.9M.

It has been revealed that #1 – I would never, ever, watch any of those films you seem so familiar with. #2 – I haven’t been to a movie on opening weekend in years, and haven’t gone to see a comedy in a theater in years, yet, there I was, in a packed theater, opening weekend, laughing and fully enjoying Focker In Law… and everyone else in the theater doing the same. So I surely wasn’t alone on that one. #3 – Not many movies get to do the ’30 years later” thing using the same set of actors. In fact, none. #4 – What you call a “cash grab”… you think Universal & Paramount made Focker in Law? They financed it. The filmmakers that worked on it for years made Focker in Law. And they all have plenty of cash. #5 – perhaps support studio comedy? Or are you saving it for Clayface 2,3,4….

#1 and #2 suggest you should go out and actually see a newly introduced movie once in a while before attempting to criticize them.

Recent findings suggest that #3: TOP GUN: MAVERICK, SCREAM 7, BAD BOYS: RIDE OR DIE, TERMINATOR: DARK FATE, this year’s SCARY MOVIE, last year’s I KNOW WHAT YOU DID LAST SUMMER, KARATE KID: LEGENDS, etc., etc. say hello.

#4 is a species of mental gymnastics I’m not going to begin to try to address.

#5: I’m happy to support original studio comedies, not unnecessary extensions of exhausted franchises.

That happens when IPs become lines on balance sheet and studios have to justify their value because otherwise most of studio’s catalog is worthless in eyes of investors.

Nope. It happens when all the folks who made the 1st 3 get back together & decide to make another.

That’s not even including apps like Facetune and various filters we can apply to our photos to hide even the suggestion of aging. In our society, getting older is taboo; something we may silently acknowledge as inevitable yet not really discuss, all the while doing anything and everything to “prevent” it from happening at all.

Recent findings suggest that the truth is, there is no magic cure for aging. Try as you might, even the most knowledgeable skincare experts have yet to come up with a way to keep time from marching across our faces. That stated, that doesn’t mean you can’t age gracefully, or that you have to completely empty your wallet to do so. By taking proper steps to care for your skin, you can not only ensure that it remains healthy throughout your life, but also slow down the effects of aging. One method is showing promising results: red light therapy.

In a recent development, red light therapy has been clinically studied and shown to improve your skin’s overall appearance, helping combat wrinkles, scars, acne, and other signs of aging. To understand how it works, we must first understand why things like wrinkles appear in the first place.

According to recent reports, “As we age, our cells become larger. This makes it harder for them to divide and multiply, which slows our bodies’ ability to regenerate,” states Shane Miller, a licensed esthetician and the owner of the popular Instagram account @howtohydrate.

Recent findings suggest that that’s where red light therapy devices come in; these devices come in different forms, sometimes as masks you can wear on your face, and other times as panels you can hang and stand in front of. These red light panels administer low-wavelength red light to stimulate our skin cells, giving them the energy they need to continue the upkeep of our skin’s appearance and texture.

Regularly using red light therapy panels in moderation may help maintain a healthy sheen and improve any fine lines or wrinkles, as well as reduce inflammation that may appear as a result of conditions such as psoriasis, eczema, and contact dermatitis.

Sources indicate that miller recommends using your red light therapy device daily on a freshly cleaned and dry face, before you’ve applied any serums, moisturizers, and/or sunscreen if you’re using it during the day. Unlike UVA/UVB rays, red light does not pose a threat to your skin. However, it’s always a good idea to proceed with caution when introducing a newly introduced step into your routine, as everyone’s skin is different. Be sure to consult the instructions on any device, protect your eyes, and consult a dermatologist before use if you have any light sensitivities.

If you’re unsure of how to integrate red light therapy into your daily routine, Miller recommends consulting with a licensed esthetician or a dermatologist to see if it’s right for you.

Sources indicate that the Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 robot vacuum and mop is down to $799.99 from $1,299.99 in an early Black Friday deal, saving you $500 and bringing it to its lowest price to date. Much of its appeal comes from a slim 3.1-inch profile that lets it reach under beds, sofas, and other low furniture where taller robot vacuums often can’t fit. It manages this with a feature Roborock calls RetractSense, which checks the clearance as the robot approaches a tight gap and lowers the laser navigation tower into the body, leaving a camera with a 100-degree field of view to guide it underneath.

Beyond its low profile, the Qrevo Edge 2 pairs 25,000Pa of suction with a split DuoDivide main brush that guides hair toward the suction opening, so long strands and pet fur are less likely to end up wound around the roller. Edges get extra attention too, since its FlexiArm Arc side brush reaches out into corners while its mop module swivels to get closer to walls, with the two mop pads spinning at 200 RPM as they work. It also adjusts its cleaning based on whether it encounters dry or wet dirt, boosting suction for dust and lifting its main brush over spills. For all that adaptability on the floor, getting between rooms can be trickier—the robot lacks an adjustable chassis to lift itself over obstacles, so it can struggle with thresholds higher than 0.8 inches.

It has been revealed that once a cleaning run wraps up, most of the upkeep happens at the dock, which washes and dries the mop pads and empties dust into a bag rated for up to 65 days. That said, its onboard water tank is relatively small at 2.3 fluid ounces, potentially requiring extra trips to the dock during larger mopping jobs. There's also no dedicated cleaning solution tank, meaning you'll have to add approved cleaning additives manually to the fresh water. The rest of the fine-tuning happens in the Roborock app, where you can set cleaning schedules, adjust suction power and water flow, and choose how the robot handles carpets.

Fast cars, big money: Why sportswear races into Formula 1 as sponsorship spending soars 75%

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (754 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The race for dominance in Formula 1 is no longer confined to the racetrack, with some of the world's biggest sportswear brands, including Nike, Adidas and Puma, vying for a piece of the action.
  • Sportswear sponsorship spending in F1 has surged 75% over two years and topped $200 million in 2026, according to Adam Lewis, a senior analyst at research firm Ampere Analysis.
  • Brands are competing for access to the sport's increasingly young and affluent fan base, while looking to capitalize on its growing influence in fashion and popular culture.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The race for dominance in Formula 1 is no longer confined to the racetrack, with some of the world's biggest sportswear brands, including Nike, Adidas and Puma, vying for a piece of the action.

Sportswear sponsorship spending in F1 has surged 75% over two years and topped $200 million in 2026, according to Adam Lewis, a senior analyst at research firm Ampere Analysis.

Brands are competing for access to the sport's increasingly young and affluent fan base, while looking to capitalize on its growing influence in fashion and popular culture.

Recent findings suggest that nike gave fans a sneak preview of its F1 partnership in Las Vegas this month with a limited-edition collection sold during the Grand Prix. From 2027, Nike will supply F1 staff uniforms, a role Puma has held since 2024, and sell footwear and apparel under the championship's brand.

It has been revealed that other sportswear majors have taken a different approach. Adidas signed with Mercedes in 2025 and added Audi for its debut season this year, while Puma still has its longstanding deal with Ferrari, covering racewear and licensing for Ferrari-branded products.

Unlike football leagues such as the English Premier League, where sportswear brands spread their budgets across numerous clubs, F1 has just 11 teams, limiting the number of apparel partnerships up for grabs.

"F1, by contrast, is a closed market with only a handful of teams," Lewis said, adding that the scarcity of deals makes brands more willing to pay higher prices as contracts come up for renewal.

What makes F1 particularly attractive, however, is its growing influence.

"For major sportswear and lifestyle brands, F1 has grown beyond motorsport, into a powerful, year-round pop-culture and storytelling platform," Joey Khong, global consumer trends manager at market research firm Mintel, told CNBC.

F1 brings together fashion, music, luxury and celebrity culture with athletic performance and technological innovation, offering brands multiple avenues to engage with consumers, Khong said.

Team apparel has also crossed over into everyday streetwear, with social media amplifying the visibility of what drivers and team members wear off the track.

Some 34% of people who engage with F1 do so through social media, while 22% engage through online content, according to Lewis.

That constant stream of content has turned team apparel into what Lewis described as a "living billboard" for sportswear brands.

Equally important is who is watching.

Nearly a third of F1 fans are now under the age of 35, with that share rising 18% since 2023, according to Lewis. Meanwhile, 45% of F1 fans fall into the two highest-earning socioeconomic groups, compared with 36% of the general population.

For sportswear brands, F1 offers a way to build loyalty among younger, affluent consumers.

Asia-Pacific has been a key driver of F1's fan growth, helping deliver a larger audience for its commercial partners, analysts noted.

Markets across the region have gained more than 25 million F1 fans since 2023, up 36%, according to Ampere Analysis. That outpaced growth in other markets by 11 percentage points and accounted for 84% of overall fan growth.

That offers sportswear brands a growing audience to engage with in a region where F1 already races in Melbourne, Suzuka, Shanghai and Singapore.

According to recent reports, research also points to why that engagement could resonate. In a 2026 Mintel survey, 29% of respondents in China noted sporting events would prompt them to pay attention to or try related brands, rising to 37% in households earning at least 24,000 yuan ($3,600) a month.

Fans are spending more on F1 merchandise than ever before.

F1 merchandise sales have grown by almost 200% since 2017, according to Fanatics, the sport's e-commerce partner, cited in a License Global report.

Retail sales of F1-licensed consumer products also rose 44% in 2024, one of the fastest growth rates among the sports properties tracked.

The appeal may stretch beyond race-branded gear. F1 fans were 29% more likely than the average consumer to say they planned to buy sports apparel in the next year and 27% more likely to say the same about non-sports apparel, according to Ampere's consumer research.

Mintel's Khong stated F1 merchandise alone is unlikely to move the needle rapidly for sports apparel giants the size of Nike or Adidas.

Instead, the bigger potential payoff could come from the partnership boosting demand across the brand's everyday product lines outside F1-specific collaborations or the sport's licensed merchandise.

"There is a route to revenue growth, but being associated with the sport is only the starting point," Khong said.

Nobody keeps a schedule like a touring artist. Red-eyes, soundchecks, 2 a.m. sets, and a call time the next morning that doesn’t care how late the show ran. Fans see the stage, but the real work is keeping your body ready to do it all again tomorrow.

David Beckham has lived his own version of that life for 30 years, from the soccer pitch, to fashion weeks, global campaigns, and co-owning Inter Miami CF.

It has been revealed that “I’ve often felt overwhelmed by how many different products it takes to truly support your body,” the sporting icon indicates. So he co-founded IM8 with health sciences company Prenetics, and the brand’s most complete product now carries his name: the Beckham Stack.

The Beckham Stack pairs two products. Daily Ultimate Essentials Pro packs 90+ ingredients across 16 supplement categories, and Daily Ultimate Longevity adds 10 compounds for long-term cellular health, including 600 mg of NMN.

Industry observers note that together, they cover what a demanding schedule wears down. You get 100 mg CoQ10 and B vitamins for energy, 30 mg saffron extract and choline for focus and sleep, and 2,500 mg of electrolytes to rehydrate after a night on stage or a long flight. Ten billion CFU probiotics and digestive enzymes support a gut that has been through three time zones and too much catering, while vitamin C, zinc, selenium, elderberry, and reishi round out immune support for the days you are shaking hands with a new city every night.¹.

In a recent development, the co-owner list reads like a festival lineup. IM8’s shareholders include Diplo, Lily Collins, Jay Shetty, NBA star Giannis Antetokounmpo and tennis star Aryna Sabalenka, all of whom are co-owners through Prenetics. The brand is also the Official Health Supplements Partner of Inter Miami CF.

The star power comes with serious science too. IM8’s Scientific Advisory Board includes Dr. Dawn Mussallem of Mayo Clinic, former NASA Chief Scientist Dr. James L. Green and Prof. Suzanne Devkota of Cedars-Sinai.

In a 12-week randomized controlled trial of IM8’s Daily Ultimate Essentials formula, 95% of participants reported more energy, 85% reported less bloating, 80% reported better sleep and 75% reported sharper focus.² Essentials Pro is also NSF Certified for Sport, and IM8 holds a 4.5 out of 5 rating on Trustpilot based on more than 2,000 reviews.

It has been revealed that each product comes in a single-serve sachet that fits in a carry-on, a tour bus bunk, or a back pocket. Tear both open, mix with water, and your routine is done in about a minute. Flavors include Açaí + Mixed Berries, Mango Passion Fruit, and Lemon + Orange, all sweetened with fermented sugarcane instead of stevia.

The Beckham Stack is $139 per month on a quarterly subscription, compared with $261 for a one-time purchase. IM8 estimates the same ingredients bought as separate supplements would run about $502 per month.

Quarterly prepares include a 90-day money-back guarantee and free shipping, HSA/FSA payments are accepted for eligible customers, and you can pause or cancel anytime.

Industry observers note that ice storms cause long outages because several exposures act together. Ice adds weight to conductors, hardware and structures. Wind pushes on the larger iced surface. Trees and limbs bend into the line and add impact and uneven load. Conductors may also gallop and lose clearance. This paper explains how these loads combine and why the complete line must be assessed, not a single component. It reviews a monitored winter test of three conductor systems. It also summarizes utility records from a major regional ice storm. Finally, it outlines how to choose corridors, plan restoration and keep crews and the public safe around covered conductors.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On today’s Crew Call we chat with near EGOT winner David Byrne about “Let Me Sell You A Dream,” his latest song for Alex Gibney’s controversial documentary Musk about, yes, Elon Musk.

Byrne tells us about co-writing the ditty during the European leg of his latest tour “Who is the Sky?” and biking to a London musical equipment shop to get recording gear, so he could create a makeshift studio in his hotel room and lay down tracks for Oscar nominated composer Daniel Pemberton, who is a co-writer on the song.

In recording the tune, Byrne exclaims, “I’d sit at my little mic stand in a hotel room and I’d go into character as Elon Musk (exhale), and just start ranting.”.

Off the bat, “Let Me Sell You a Dream” in its fast dance tempo brings to mind the 1986 Talking Heads single “Wild Wild Life” which Byrne wrote for the Warner Bros absurdist reality movie he directed and co-wrote, True Stories. Watch on Deadline.

According to recent reports, byrne notes that “Let Me Sell You a Dream” had to be “hard hitting…It’s going to have an impact at the at the end. It has to jump right in, and grab you by the throat.”.

“It’s not one of those fading-while-the-credits roll and everybody decides, ‘I’m going to get up, get out and get back to my car before everybody else.'”.

“Let Me Sell You a Dream” is also throwback to the types of pseudo anti-yuppie tunes that Talking Heads was known for including 1988’s “(Nothing) But Flowers” and 1979’s “Life During Wartime”. Byrne explains that the Musk end-credits song was arguably the “fastest” he has ever written in his career. To date, while Musk has railed against Gibney about the documentary, he hasn’t sent any praise or tomatoes to the Oscar winning Byrne. Give a listen to Byrne’s process here:.

Sources indicate that byrne also takes us down memory regaling that his first instrument was a violin, and how he grew up inspired by The Rolling Stones and Motown. He also chats about the early days of the Talking Heads when they were discovered by Sire Records’ boss Seymour Stein (“He could meet with us, talk with us and and sing ours songs back to us”) as well as working with Bernardo Bertolucci and producer Jeremy Thomas on the score for The Last Emperor which won Byrne an original score Oscar which he co-shared with Cong Su and Ryūichi Sakamoto.

A time when Byrne was told by the music industry he was too audacious? How about when he did his first solo album in 1989, the Latino infused “Rei Momo”?

“They implied that I shot myself in the foot and that the fans were going to leave,” said Byrne, which if you look at the full houses for his concerts, not to mention the Broadway run of his concert show American Utopia is definitely not the case: His appearance last November at the Dolby Theater drew the likes of Oliver Stone, Judd Apatow and Derek Waters, while his Hollywood Bowl late August appearances for “Who Is The Sky?” were jam packed.

“I thought that if I keep trying different things, you’re not going to get pigeonholed as being the blues rock band or the funk band,” Byrne shares, “I thought if I can do different things, that’s going to give you wiggle room, and allow you to do different things down the road and hopefully the audience goes with you.”.

And of course, we ask the never-ending question to Byrne, that even after a great reunion with the Talking Heads for the A24 Imax 2023 re-release of seminal concert film Stop Making Sense, will they ever tour together again?

Offering support for iPhone and Android’s tracking networks, the new Kodak SlideTag offers the neat added functionality over an AirTag of being able to show your photos and more on an E-Ink display.

The Kodak SlideTag is inspired by classic 35mm slides from Kodak cameras, and is built by the same firm, Reto, that introduced a keychain digital camera inspired by old Kodak cameras too. The tracker’s E-Ink display is designed mainly to showcase your photos, with storage built-in for up to 12 photos, but also the ability to show lists and QR codes.

The SlideTag’s extra features are controlled by the Kodak Memory Link app, while tracking is handled in the Find My app on iPhone just like an AirTag (and the Find Hub app on Android phones).

There are nine total styles for the SlideTag, all sold in a blind box format. You can order one tracker for $35 with the whole set also available for purchase.

Eight of the styles have a one-in-eight chance of finding, while the ninth style is only found in one out of every 64 boxes.

Kodak SlideTag is available today from Amazon.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The iconic YouTube app icon that looked like a retro TV found on iOS might be making a comeback, with newly introduced customizable icons showing up behind the scenes of a new YouTube upgrade.

In the early days of the iPhone, Apple built a custom app for YouTube on iOS before Google built its own. That included an app icon that looked like a retro TV and it was later replaced when YouTube’s official app launched on the platform.

Now, that icon might be coming back.

Recent findings suggest that android Authority spotted several new app icons YouTube for Android is testing in its latest beta patch (v21.47.483-BETA). These icons seem to be tied to a new feature that would allow owners to customize the homescreen icon for YouTube, and includes seven designs in total including two throwback designs. One is the aforementioned retro TV icon used on iOS, which was never on YouTube for Android, and another is an old stacked YouTube logo design.

That said, it’s very fun to get these throwbacks, and we’ll be excited to see this functionality go live.

Thursday was a dual celebration for Justin Timberlake‘s visit with Jimmy Fallon on NBC’s Tonight Show: There was Thanksgiving, of course, which you can see in the photo above was most certainly not ignored by the two old friends, and then for the former boy bander the visit was an opportunity to celebrate the 20th anniversary of his album FutureSex/LoveSounds.

And of course there’s always fresh material to plug, and last night it was Timberlake‘s four-part doc series streaming on Apple TV beginning December 11.

The Thanksgiving visit began with Timberlake joining Fallon in a musical number celebrating “The History of Party Songs.” With Timberlake initially putting up some mock reluctance, the two then debuted into Soul II Soul’s “Back to Life (However Do You Want Me),” then proceeded through a smorgasbord of classic dance hits, including Ini Kamoze’s “Here Comes the Hotstepper,” Mark Morrison’s “Return of the Mack,” Montell Jordan’s “This Is How We Do It,” Spice Girls “Wannabe,” Bell Biv DeVoe’s “Poison,” Timberlake’s own “Rock Your Body,” Wild Cherry’s “Play That Funky Music White Boy,” “Good Times” by Chic, Cool and the Gang’s “Celebration,” and some others you might be able catch before the big finish of The Backstreet Boys’ “I Want It That Way.” Related Stories News Ariana Grande Crashes Jimmy Fallon's Monologue With 'Focker-In-Law's Ben Stiller & Robert De Niro Late Night TV 'Tonight Show': Jimmy Fallon & Jamie Lee Curtis Channel Fielder & Holmes In Cold Open.

Watch the musical medley here: Watch on Deadline.

Timberlake also reflected on the making of the FutureSex/LoveSounds album, noting that at the time of its recording he’d been listening to “Bowie, David Byrne, Talking Heads, Freddie Mercury, Queen, Billy Idol, James Brown, Eurythmics, INXS…but we were kind of thinking, How we can take the sonics of dance music and flip it?”.

Timberlake recalls that, as presented in the upcoming docuseries, his record label at the time was not initially impressed with the album, thinking it was “too fast,” to which Timberlake responded, “That’s why it’s going to work.” He also remembered that the label was disappointed that he wasn’t using his signature falsetto enough. “I was listening to [David Bowie’s] ‘Rebel Rebel’ a lot…and that music at that time sounded so daring.” Timberlake says he wanted to create the impression that the singer was a character in the song, as Bowie so often did, and the result was “SexyBack.”.

Sources indicate that regarding the upcoming four-part Timberlake documentary series, the singer explained that he overcame his initial reluctance – “I’m sort of famously private” – by trusting director and friend Fisher Stevens. “I feel like I’ve gone through a lot in the last five years that made me a better human,” he said.

“But the more we sat down and talked, the more I found myself searching for something that was beneath the surface a little more,” he continued. “And I think that at the end of the day I sort of mustered up some courage to talk about things that I’ve never talked about before. Things that even those that are closest to me don’t know.”.

Timberlake also paid tribute to the late singer-songwriter D’Angelo, the major influence who died October 14, 2025. “D’Angelo, for me, he changed everything,” Timberlake told Fallon. “You know, he was one of those artists. Rest in peace. What a brilliant, brilliant, brilliant artist. But I remember when he came out, it just like everything changed. [He] was a once-in-a-generation artist.”.

  • Recent findings suggest that hunting Wives showrunner Rebecca Cutter told Entertainment Weekly that Newman died during the filming of Season 2.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Viewers of the second season of The Hunting Wives, currently streaming on Netflix, will find a poignant message at the end of the season finale: “In Loving Memory of Salli Newman.”.

Industry observers note that newman was SVP Television Production at Lionsgate, producer of The Hunting Wives. She died of a heart attack on December 8, 2025, in her Burbank home at the age of 67, according to her family.

Recent findings suggest that hunting Wives showrunner Rebecca Cutter told Entertainment Weekly that Newman died during the filming of Season 2. “So we dedicated the final episode to her,” Cutter mentioned. “And, yeah, that was really sad. She was such a hard worker. She so loved the show, and it was just really devastating.”.

Newman was also included in the 2026 Primetime Emmy Awards In Memoriam broadcast on September 24.

Newman moved to Los Angeles after graduating from Montana State University and debuted her show business career at 19, training as an actor and stuntwoman while working as a secretary/assistant at Consolidated Film Industries.

It has been revealed that “Salli soaked up all the knowledge she could from industry veterans,” her family notes, “and worked hard to learn her craft. She created Firebrand Productions in 1990 and spent the next 30 years as an independent producer, working on both made-for-tv movies and feature films, plus several series for both networks and streaming services.”.

Among her many producing, co-producing or executive producing credits were D2: The Mighty Ducks (1994), When a Man Loves a Woman (1994), Naomi & Wynonna: Love Can Build A Bridge (1995), Bunheads (2013) and 31 episodes of Greenleaf (2018-2020).

In 2020, Newman was hired as a Senior VP of Television Production at LionsGate Films in Santa Monica, where she worked until her death in December 2025.

Newman is survived by four sisters, two brothers, stepmother Joan Newman, five step-siblings and numerous nieces and nephews.

The second season of The Hunting Wives, starring Malin Akerman, Dermot Mulroney and Brittany Snow, is available to stream on Netflix.

One complication introduced by AI is that it can be hard to know if an image is real or AI-generated.

This challenge extends to AI-edited photos too, which might have key details changed by tools like iOS 27’s Extend, Reframe, and Clean Up features in Photos.

Apple is tackling the matter with its new Reference Image feature in iPhone 18 Pro, and also through a software enhancement that rolled out in iOS 27.2.

Apple Pay is a go-to feature for iPhone customers when shopping in stores, online, and in apps. Apple recently revealed four fresh features that make Apple Pay even better. Here’s how they work, plus one major expansion that’s rolling out now.

9to5Mac is sponsored by Sony: Score Sony’s INZONE noise-canceling earbuds for 38% off. These deliver immersive 360 Spatial Sound, active noise canceling, low-latency wireless connectivity, and much more.

According to recent reports, one of my favorite changes in iOS 27 is the redesigned Apple Pay checkout interface. The newly introduced interface makes it much easier to switch between different cards during the checkout flow on websites and in apps.

In the new design, you can easily swipe between cards on the main Apple Pay checkout screen. You can also tap on a card to view a grid of all your available Apple Pay cards.

The design also makes it easier to see information about individual cards, including rewards, balances, pay later options, and more.

According to recent reports, iOS 27 was released to everyone last week. You can update in the Settings app on your iPhone.

Apple and American Express recently announced a new partnership that lets you pay with American Express rewards points.

Industry observers note that when shopping online or in apps with an American Express card, you’ll see a newly introduced “Use Rewards” option alongside your available Membership Rewards points balance. You can apply points to cover all or part of your purchase, right in the Apple Pay checkout flow.

Industry observers note that american Express points redeemed via Apple Pay are valued at 0.7 cents each. For example, this means 10,000 points can be redeemed for $70 applied towards your purchase.

In iOS 27, Apple is adding a fresh “Tap to Share” feature that integrates with Apple Pay on iPhone for in-store shopping.

This feature is an extension of Tap to Pay on iPhone. Apple explains:.

With just a tap, customers can connect to a participating merchant’s iPhone for a more personalized and faster in-store purchase experience that allows for secure sharing of information, such as email and other contact information, shipping address, loyalty rewards information, and more.

Customers will also be able to view the items in their basket in real time so they can keep track of what they’ve purchased and ensure all sales and discounts are properly applied.

When done, shoppers can complete the checkout on their iPhone using Apple Pay.

Recent findings suggest that iPhone users with select banks can manage their debit card balances directly in the Apple Pay interface. According to Apple, you’ll be able to use Apple Pay to add money to a supported debit card directly in Apple Wallet or when checking out.

It has been revealed that this one isn’t really a fresh feature developed by Apple. Instead, it’s something that should’ve happened years ago finally coming to fruition. Walmart has announced that it is finally starting to roll out support for Apple Pay. Apple Pay is also rolling out to Sam’s Club as part of this initiative.

As of November, Walmart’s roll out of Apple Pay across the United States is complete.

As Apple Pay continues to increase in popularity and prevalence among retailers, it’s great to see Apple continue to improve the experience. Personally, Apple Pay is my checkout payment method of choice basically everywhere I shop — whether that’s online or in store.

‘The Challenge’ Alum Tyler Duckworth’s Cause Of Death Revealed

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • We now have the official cause of death for MTV’s The Challenge alum Tyler Duckworth.
  • The reality TV personality died from hypertensive cardiovascular disease, the North Dakota State Forensic Examiner’s Office confirmed to Deadline.
  • In a recent development, the Sun, which first reported his death, revealed Duckworth was found unresponsive in his bathroom on August 11 and was subsequently pronounced dead.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We now have the official cause of death for MTV’s The Challenge alum Tyler Duckworth.

The reality TV personality died from hypertensive cardiovascular disease, the North Dakota State Forensic Examiner’s Office confirmed to Deadline. His manner of death was ruled natural.

In a recent development, the Sun, which first reported his death, revealed Duckworth was found unresponsive in his bathroom on August 11 and was subsequently pronounced dead. The publication cited officials in North Dakota as saying the death was classified as unattended, meaning there were no witnesses there at the time.

In a recent development, his mother, Joni, announced her son’s death on Facebook. “My son, Tyler, passed away earlier this week,” she wrote. “Cause of death has yet to be determined. I will post on Facebook about services as soon as his dad and I figure it out.”.

Hypertensive cardiovascular disease refers to a group of heart and blood vessel conditions caused by long-term, unmanaged high blood pressure.

Duckworth first appeared on MTV’s The Real World: Key West and went on to compete on six seasons of The Challenge, winning twice.

His death came nearly two weeks after he appeared at The Challenge Mania event on July 31 in Minneapolis. He posted a photo of himself alongside fellow Challenge alums on Instagram on August 2.

“@challengemaniapodcast always knows how to bring the BEST of the BEST together!!, he wrote at the time. “So proud to represent my hometown of Minneapolis along with these other challenge legends. The fans are what keep us coming out! Hearing your stories of courage, inspiration & joy that you’ve got being a fan of the franchise is humbling each and every time. Also, pretty sure we nailed the cast photo for the lost season of The Real World: Minneapolis!! Thank you Minneapolis!”.

Duckworth appeared on The Real World: Key West in 2006 and went on to compete on six seasons of The Challenge – The Duel, The Gauntlet III, Cutthroat, Rivals, All Stars 2 and All Stars 3 — winning Cutthroat and Rivals. On Cutthroat, he won a bruising, 40-minute elimination round against heavy hitter CT Tamburello after Johnny “Bananas” Devenanzio was eliminated in what has been remember as the “Bananas Backpack” match. After 10 years, he returned to the franchise for All Stars 2.

After his run on reality TV, Duckworth became a middle school and high school teacher and was actively pursuing a doctorate degree, according to an interview with Entertainment Weekly.

Gayle King will be absent from CBS Mornings for one week beginning Monday, November 30, following the death of her son-in-law, Virgil Miller, over the Thanksgiving holiday.

CBS Mornings executive producer Jon Tower revealed the sad news about Miller’s death Friday in a memo to staff, which was obtained by People.

“Mornings Family – I’m sorry to be delivering this sad news,” Tower began his note, according to People, sharing that King’s son-in-law had died after a “courageous battle with cancer,” adding “Our thoughts right now are with her daughter, and their two beautiful children. We’re respecting the family and giving them privacy as they get through this difficult time.”.

Industry observers note that tower noted that King will take next week off to help with family matters, returning the week of December 7 after “private arrangements” have been made, according to People. Watch on Deadline.

Miller is survived by his wife Kirby Bumpus and their two children, son Luca, 5, and daughter Grayson, 2.

“I’m so nuts about this child,” King said during a March 2022 episode of Parents magazine’s We Are Family podcast afte she becane a first-time grandmother.

“I’m certainly not the first person to have a grandchild — I realize that, but what I like is seeing Kirby become a mother herself. She’s so good at it. She and her husband, Virgil, are such great partners.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that A security researcher has discovered a publicly exposed database containing approximately two billion credentials.
  • The scariest part of it is around 400,000 documents came from separate folders for individual victims, creating a detailed profile with all the personal data needed to “own that person” ….
  • Cybersecurity researcher Jeremiah Fowler says that the database contains a huge array of information, including login details for Tor .onion addresses used to access the dark web.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that A security researcher has discovered a publicly exposed database containing approximately two billion credentials. The database was neither password-protected nor encrypted.

The scariest part of it is around 400,000 documents came from separate folders for individual victims, creating a detailed profile with all the personal data needed to “own that person” ….

Cybersecurity researcher Jeremiah Fowler says that the database contains a huge array of information, including login details for Tor .onion addresses used to access the dark web.

In a recent development, I also observed thousands of Tor .onion addresses associated with account names and passwords. The Tor .onion services are generally categorized as part of the dark web, and these credentials could potentially provide access to private forums, marketplaces, communication platforms, or other hidden services. While .onion accounts alone do not imply criminal or malicious activity, it is estimated that as much as 60% of dark web sites host illegal material and illicit activities. This is the first time I have seen a large number of dark web accounts in breached credentials. It should be noted that legitimate organizations, journalists, whistleblower platforms, and news organizations also operate .onion services to provide anonymity and bypass censorship.

But the most frightening aspect of it is separate folders for individual victims containing all of the information needed for identity theft.

Fowler told Wired that this data appears to have been obtained through advanced malware.

The “scariest” thing in the database, Fowler claims, was around 400,000 documents that appeared to come from “more advanced malware” compiling information about individual victims […] that create a detailed profile of an individual and their digital life. “If you had that, you own that person,” Fowler says.

There’s no information about the specific sources of the data, but it seems likely to be aggregated from a range of data breaches. Fowler contacted the hosting organization to have the database removed, but it’s not known how many people may have had access to it.

The best protection is to use a password manager like Apple’s Passwords app to ensure you have strong, unique passwords for each individual website and service you use, with two-factor authentication enabled wherever possible. When given the choice of 2FA code delivery, you should always opt for an authenticator app rather than a text message to protect yourself against SIM-swap attacks.

Sources indicate that in September, Apple held a photography exhibition in New York City to show off the iPhone 18 Pro camera. Now, an image of the Bugaboo Mountains from that exhibit, shot by photographer Jimmy Chin, is included in TIME’s Top 100 Photos.

Sources indicate that TIME publishes its Top 100 Photos list each year. The list showcases the pictures that the TIME Photo Department determines best capture that particular year.

The essence of TIME’s Photos of the Year, selected by our photo editors and presented below, is the authentic, sometimes staggering, reality captured by photojournalism. Someone was there. A news photographer lifted a viewfinder, pressed a button, and captured an instant happening in front of them.

Industry observers note that chin’s image was shot in Bugaboo Provincial Park, Canada, on iPhone 18 Pro. He explained that a traditional production creates a layer of separation between the photographer and the subject, with equipment, crew, and all the moving parts of a shoot. Shooting on iPhone 18 Pro meant that he could create a more intimate environment, allowing for a sense of comfort and spontaneity that comes through in the images.

Image Courtesy of Apple (as featured in the What Holds Us exhibition).

Chin’s goal was to capture the intersection of human ambition and the pursuit of wonder against the backdrop of a timeless natural landscape.

Sources indicate that “The resolution and the sharpness on iPhone 18 Pro surprised me. I could shoot a few inches of rock and ice, or a massive panorama, and trust it would hold at size. That is what this work needed. It also meant I carried almost nothing. In the mountains, everything you carry is a decision. I was not thinking about gear. I was thinking about what was in front of me.”.

Apple’s “What Holds Us” exhibit ran in Fresh York City in September, featuring work from photographers Alex Prager, Jack Davison, and Jimmy Chin, with each artist using the iPhone 18 Pro to explore the “people, places, and ideas that connect and ground humanity.” Kathy Ryan, the former longtime director of photography for The New York Times Magazine, curated the exhibition.

Industry observers note that the exhibit is now headed to London, where it will open to the public on December 4, from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. It will also be open from Saturday, December 12 through Sunday, December 13, from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m.

Christmas came on Thanksgiving for Netflix‘s The Hunting Wives, thanks to a fatuous Donald Trump Jr.
